title: Scam or fine?
instruction: You got these messages. Which ones are scams?

items.text: A friend on Discord: “I’m giving away skins, log in here: game-skins-free.net”
items.why: A strange page wants your login. And your friend’s account may have been stolen.

items.text: The game’s official app: “You have a reward in your inventory for finishing the week.”
items.why: It doesn’t want anything from you. You find the reward yourself, right in the game.

items.text: A “moderator”: “Send me the code from your SMS, we’ll verify your account.”
items.why: Never give an SMS code to anyone. No moderator needs it.

items.text: An unknown player: “I’ll sell you a rare sword, send the money first.”
items.why: Money in advance to a stranger, outside the game’s shop. The sword will most likely never arrive.

items.text: An e-mail: “Your account will be deleted within an hour, click and confirm your password.”
items.why: Fear and hurry at once. Log in yourself through the app and see whether anything is going on.

items.text: A classmate at school shows you a skin they bought in the game’s shop
items.why: Nobody wants anything from you, and the game’s shop is official.

debrief: A scam gives itself away by what it wants from you: a password, a code or money, and right now. Check it another way.
